title: ALMA-IMF. I. Investigating the origin of stellar masses: Introduction to the Large Program and first results
question: Investigate the origin of the initial mass function (IMF) of stars and whether the core mass function (CMF) varies with cloud characteristics and evolutionary stage across 15 massive Galactic protoclusters.

recipe.goal: Select sample of 15 massive Galactic protoclusters and estimate central clump and cloud masses from ATLASGAL 870 μm data
recipe.method: Apply distance (2-5.5 kpc), Galactic longitude (excluding 355° < l < 5°), and 870 μm flux (>25 Jy, plus W43-MM3 and G328.25) criteria to the Csengeri et al. (2017) ATLASGAL catalog, rebalance for IR-quiet vs IR-bright stages, and compute optically thin dust masses using Eq. (1).
assumptions: Optically thin thermal dust emission; κ_870μm = 0.0185 cm^2 g^-1; gas-to-dust ratio = 100; T_dust = 20 K (IR-quiet / Young), 25 K (Intermediate), 30 K (IR-bright / Evolved)

recipe.goal: Produce 1.3 mm and 3 mm continuum mosaics (bsens and cleanest) and preliminary spectral line cubes
recipe.method: Combine 12 m array configurations and image with tclean using Briggs robust = 0 in the ALMA-IMF reduction pipeline, producing bsens (all channels) and cleanest (line-free channels) continuum mosaics as well as line cubes.
key_parameters: robust = 0; spectral index α = 3.5; central frequencies ν_B6 = 228.965 GHz, ν_B3 = 100.713 GHz; FOV down to 15% primary beam sensitivity
assumptions: Spectral index α = 3.5 corresponding to optically thin dust emission with emissivity index β = 1.5

recipe.goal: Classify protocluster evolutionary stages (Young, Intermediate, Evolved) using 1.3 mm / 3 mm flux ratios and H41α free-free surface density
recipe.method: Integrate 1.3 mm and 3 mm bsens continuum fluxes over A_1.3mm to compute S^cloud_1.3mm / S^cloud_3mm, integrate H41α cubes clipped at 5σ to derive free-free continuum flux surface density Σ^free-free_H41α via Eq. (2), and visually inspect three-color (1.3 mm, 3 mm, H41α) images.
assumptions: Local thermodynamical equilibrium (LTE); T_e = 8000 K; N_He/N_H = 0.08; cloud dust emissivity index β = 1.8

recipe.goal: Extract compact cores, compute core masses and sizes, and analyze core population properties
recipe.method: Extract sources from cleanest 1.3 mm continuum images using getsf (Paper III), exclude free-free emission peaks, compute individual and cumulative core masses using Eq. (3), compare with thermal Bonnor-Ebert mass Eq. (4), and test correlation between cloud mass and maximum core mass using Spearman's rank correlation.
key_parameters: Bright core flux threshold = 400 mJy * (3.9 kpc / d)^2
assumptions: Optically thin thermal dust emission; κ_1.3mm = 0.01 cm^2 g^-1; gas-to-dust ratio = 100; T_dust = 20 K for most cores and T_dust = 75 K for the 10 brightest cores; gas-to-star conversion efficiency = 50% for high-mass star precursors (>16 M_sun)

recipe.goal: Quantify gas mass concentration from clouds (1 pc) to clumps/filaments (0.1 pc) to cores (0.01 pc)
recipe.method: Integrate 1.3 mm flux over the imaged cloud area (excluding regions dominated by free-free emission as traced by H41α) to compute recovered mass M^recovered_1.3mm at T_dust = 20 K, and compute mass ratios M^recovered_1.3mm / M^cloud_870μm, M^cores_1.3mm / M^recovered_1.3mm, and M^cores_1.3mm / M^cloud_870μm.
assumptions: T_dust = 20 K and κ_1.3mm = 0.01 cm^2 g^-1 for M^recovered_1.3mm across all evolutionary stages

recipe.goal: Demonstrate cloud kinematics in G353.41 and hot core COM line richness in G351.77
recipe.method: Fit a single Gaussian to the isolated hyperfine satellite of N2H+ (1-0) (J F1 F = 1 0 1 -> 0 1 2 at ~93.176 GHz) in G353.41 to map centroid velocity and velocity width; extract full Band 3 and Band 6 spectra toward the brightest hot core in G351.77 (IRAS 17233-3606) and inspect bright cores for COM transitions.
